title: Building a pairing
subtitle: A method for any table
objectives: Analyse a dish before choosing a wine
Pair with confidence for a full meal

steps.title: Start with the dish
steps.body: Look at the dominant elements, not the main ingredient. Chicken in cream sauce is about fat and richness; chicken with lemon and herbs is about acidity. The sauce, the cooking method and the seasoning often matter more than the meat or fish itself.
steps.highlight: Pair the sauce, not the protein

steps.title: Match or contrast
steps.body: You can match, like a rich oaked Chardonnay with lobster in butter, or contrast, like a crisp Champagne cutting through fried food. High acidity and bubbles act like a squeeze of lemon, cleaning the palate of fat and salt. Tannin works similarly with fatty red meat, which softens it.
steps.highlight: Acid and bubbles cut fat; tannin loves fat

steps.prompt: Why does a tannic red work well with a fatty steak?
steps.explanation: Fat coats the mouth and tannin binds with protein and fat, so each softens the other.

steps.body: When in doubt, ask where the dish comes from. Regional pairings grew up together over centuries, like Muscadet with oysters or Chianti with tomato-based pasta.

steps.prompt: Put the steps of choosing a wine for a dish in order.
steps.explanation: Start with what's on the plate, rule out clashes, then fine-tune the style.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Pair the dominant elements, especially the sauce
Match richness or contrast with acidity and bubbles
Regional pairings are a safe starting point
